biological.citation: Harris et al. 2021 - Disruption of RFX family transcription factors causes autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, intellectual disability, and dysregulated behavior (PMID: 33658631)
biological.summary: De novo deleterious RFX3, RFX4 and RFX7 variants were found in individuals with ASD, intellectual disability and/or ADHD. RFX3 is strongly expressed in developing and adult human brain, and X-box motifs and RFX ChIP-seq peaks are enriched in the cis-regulatory regions of known ASD risk genes.
biological.sample_size: 38 individuals from 33 unrelated families (RFX3, RFX4, RFX7 combined)

biological.citation: Multi-omic analysis of the ciliogenic transcription factor RFX3 reveals a role in promoting activity-dependent responses via enhancing CREB binding in human neurons (PMID: 40060598)
biological.summary: In human iPSC-derived neurons and forebrain organoids, biallelic RFX3 loss disrupted ciliary gene expression and delayed neuronal differentiation. Monoallelic loss disrupted synaptic gene expression and activity-dependent transcription. RFX3 binding sites co-localized with CREB sites, and RFX3 deficiency decreased CREB binding and impaired induction of CREB targets after depolarization.

biological.citation: The transcription factor Rfx3 regulates beta-cell differentiation, function, and glucokinase expression (PMID: 20413507)
biological.summary: Rfx3-/- and pancreas-specific Rfx3 knockout mice showed incompletely differentiated beta-cells with reduced insulin, Glut2 and Gck, and adults were glucose intolerant. Rfx3 knockdown in Min6 cells impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Rfx3 binds the Pal-1 and Pal-2 elements of the glucokinase neuroendocrine promoter in Min6 cells and human islets.

biological.citation: RFX3 is essential for the generation of functional human pancreatic islets from stem cells (PMID: 40263183)
biological.summary: RFX3 is highly expressed in endocrine populations during iPSC-derived islet differentiation. CRISPR RFX3 KO reduced hormone-positive cells and impaired beta cell function and insulin secretion. KO also increased enterochromaffin cell specification, TXNIP levels and apoptosis, and RFX3 overexpression rescued the dysregulated genes.

biological.citation: A deficiency in RFX3 causes hydrocephalus associated with abnormal differentiation of ependymal cells (PMID: 16930429)
biological.summary: RFX3 is strongly expressed in ciliated ependymal cells of the subcommissural organ, choroid plexus and ventricular walls. Rfx3-deficient mice develop hydrocephalus with choroid plexus differentiation defects, SCO agenesis and reduced SCO-spondin expression from E14.5.

biological.citation: The transcription factor RFX3 directs nodal cilium development and left-right asymmetry specification (PMID: 15121860)
biological.summary: Rfx3 is expressed in ciliated node cells. Rfx3-deficient mice show stunted nodal cilia, left-right asymmetry defects, embryonic lethality and situs inversus. RFX3 regulates expression of D2lic, an intraflagellar transport gene.

biological.citation: RFX3 governs growth and beating efficiency of motile cilia in mouse and controls the expression of genes involved in human ciliopathies (PMID: 19671664)
biological.summary: In primary multiciliated cultures from Rfx3-/- mouse brain, motile cilia growth and beating were impaired. RFX3 is required for optimal FOXJ1 expression and binds directly to axonemal dynein gene promoters.

biological.citation: RFX3 modulation of FOXJ1 regulation of cilia genes in the human airway epithelium (PMID: 23822649)
biological.summary: RFX3 and FOXJ1 interact by immunoprecipitation in human airway basal cells. RFX3 alone did not induce cilia genes, but it acted as a co-activator that enhanced FOXJ1-driven cilia gene promoter activity and mRNA expression.

biological.citation: Auto-fatty acylation of transcription factor RFX3 regulates ciliogenesis (PMID: 30127002)
biological.summary: RFX3 is S-fatty acylated at a conserved cysteine in its dimerization domain, through enzyme-independent auto-acylation with a preference for stearic and oleic acid. A fatty acylation-deficient mutant had reduced homodimerization and failed to promote ciliary gene expression and ciliogenesis, and it impaired Hedgehog signaling.

biological.citation: CircRFX3 Up-regulates Its Host Gene RFX3 to Facilitate Tumorigenesis and Progression of Glioma (PMID: 35416616)
biological.summary: CircRFX3 recruits HNRNPK to stabilize RFX3 mRNA in glioma cells. RFX3 in turn promotes PROX1 transcription, driving glioma cell malignancy and tumor growth.
